newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian forex market closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian forex market closed for holiday.

text.p: The Malaysian foreign exchange market is closed on Friday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha celebrations.
However, the Malaysian currency is widely expected to weaken on Friday on selling by U.S. speculative funds in the overseas markets.
These funds have been building huge dollar positions against the ringgit for the last two weeks.
On Thursday, the ringgit closed at 2.5128/38 to a dollar at close of trading in Kuala Lumpur on Friday. It closed trading for Thursday in London and New York at 2.5130.
"The market still fears Bank Negara's intervention, but the funds may take advantage of the holiday on Friday and hit the ringgit," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said on Thursday.
Bank Negara intervened in the market last week at 2.5120 to slow down the ringgit's fall.
A dealer with a Malaysian bank said dollar/ringgit could be headed towards 2.52 to a dollar in the near-term.
"I do not see it (dollar/ringgit) crossing 2.5250," said Jimmy Koh, economist with I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
"Some people are talking about 2.54/55 levels. To reach that there should be something fundamentally wrong with the Malaysian economy, which there is not," he said.
